chapter: Dance tastes, big bands and the boat
title: Why his Dixieland drew crowds in New York and a Harrisburg engagement
summary: DeDroit says playing popular tunes in Dixieland style set his band apart in New York, and recalls a final engagement in Harrisburg and his policy on old tunes.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: go on forever. Were you conscious that the people here through the years had a different musical taste than in other parts of the country, that you were playing something really quite different than what people would be listening to say in Chicago or Los Angeles?
Well in the Balkan age we play strictly Dixieland, you know. But we play popular tunes in Dixieland style. Sure. Sure. And the fact that we packed the place, they must have liked it.
Something different, something new, pretty much of them. Well of course I was different.

And I made my point to be entirely different than the other band. See? But fortunately for me the other band couldn't play like we played. I mean they may have had it but they had never done it. In fact they were fine fellas. Some of them came down here to the normal street shows and I'd go over and see them, you know. In fact when my pianist got sick in Harrisburg, he operated on for appendix, I used to bring a man from New York. You know, I went up there, I bet they had a dance hall hall hall. And they wanted something outstanding. So Vincent Lopez sent me and I was coming home. That was the week I was supposed to come to New Orleans. So we finished. The last note we played was in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania. Beautiful ballroom. And we did make some money. And there were musicians, they were good musicians, but they had their way of playing. We had our way of playing. I'd play a tune and he'd say to me, the other leaders said, that's an old tune. And I'd say yes, but it's not an old tune. The tunes are the old good, you know, if they're good. And if they do something for your band, play them. And I always made a policy. If a guy liked the tune, I'll feed you tomorrow. If you liked it, he'd play the day. That's all. . . . .
